text: The clamor of the excited spectators gradually fades behind you as you venture ever deeper into the gloom of the cave tunnel. Large crystals hang from the tunnel ceiling at intervals of 20 meters, radiating a soft light, just enough for you to see where you are going. As your eyes gradually adjust to the near darkness, you begin to see movement around you. Spiders and beetles climb up and down the carved walls, disappearing into cracks and crevices as they sense your approach; rats and mice scurry across the floor ahead of you. Drops of water fall into small puddles with a sinister dripping sound that echoes through the tunnel. The air is cold, damp and heavy. After walking slowly through the tunnel for about five minutes, you arrive at a stone table set against the wall to your left. On it there are six boxes, one of which has your name painted on the lid.

choices.text: Open the box with your name on it

text: The Scorpion manages to hold you in its pincers long enough to swing its segmented tail forward, over its head, and drive its venomous stinger into you. The effect is fatal, and you collapse on the floor of the Death Arena, wondering whether Throm will manage to win.

The Gnome shakes his head and says: "I'm afraid you have not passed the Trial of Champions. The secrets of Baron Sukumvit's Deathtrap Dungeon will remain hidden for another year, as you will not be permitted to leave here. You have been appointed to be my servant for the rest of your days; you will prepare and modify the underground for future competitors. Perhaps in another life you will succeed..."
You crawl along the ground and find yourself in the lair of a tribe of TROGLODYTES. As you crawl past them, your scabbard strikes a rock. Test your Luck.

luckTest.description: You try to sneak past the Troglodytes without being noticed.

text: Knowing that the Manticore will fire the spines from its tail, you run to take cover behind one of the pillars. Before you can get there, a volley of spines flies through the air, and one of them pierces your arm. You lose 2 STAMINA points. If you are still alive, waste no time and attack the Manticore with your sword before it can fire more spines.

Still running as fast as you can, you reach into your backpack and pull out the wooden tube. Your plan is to stay underwater, breathing through the tube. With luck, the Troglodytes will think you have been swept to your death downstream, as the torrent disappears into the depths of the mountain. You hold the tube between your teeth and plunge into the water. Holding on to one of the bridge pillars underwater, you remain absolutely still for 10 minutes. When you finally think the Troglodytes have gone, you surface and look around. There is nobody in sight, and you climb out of the river and cross the bridge to the north bank. Any remaining Provisions you may have had are now soaked and useless. Cross them off your Adventure Sheet. You follow the vast cavern until, at last, you see a tunnel in the far wall. You walk up to a heavy wooden door, which is locked.

choices.text: Use the iron key on the door
Try to find another way out

text: The door opens into a large candlelit room filled with the most extraordinary lifelike statues of warriors and knights. A white-haired old man, dressed in tattered rags, leaps out from behind one of the statues and begins to giggle. A glint in his eyes makes you think that something lurks behind that idiotic appearance. In a shrill voice he says: "Well, another stone for my garden. I'm glad you've come to join your friends. I am a fair man, so I will ask you one question. If you answer correctly, you will go free — but if your answer is wrong, I will turn you to stone!" He giggles again, obviously delighted by your arrival.

After walking through the tunnel for a few minutes, you arrive at a crossroads. A white arrow painted on the wall points west. On the ground, you see wet footprints made by those who entered before you. It is hard to be sure, but it seems that three of them followed the direction of the arrow, while one decided to go east.

The lid of the box comes off easily. Inside, you find two Gold Pieces and a note written on a small piece of parchment, addressed to you. After putting the gold in your pocket, you read the message: "Well done. At least you have the good sense to stop and take advantage of the token help that is given to you. Now, I can warn you of the need to find and use several items if you hope to fare well in my Deathtrap Dungeon." Signed "Sukumvit." Committing the note's warning to memory, you tear it into small pieces and continue north through the tunnel.

As soon as you appear at the tunnel exit, a crowd screams and cheers. The people part to let you make your way towards a small podium, on which, seated beneath a colorful bamboo parasol, sits Baron Sukumvit. He looks dumbfounded, as if he never expected anyone to make it out of the Deathtrap Dungeon alive. The secret of Fang has been revealed. As the Baron rises from his chair, you climb the steps of the podium, bow before him and observe those cold eyes fixed on you in complete astonishment. You smile awkwardly as he offers you his outstretched hand. Amid the deafening roar of the people of Fang's ovation, Baron Sukumvit opens the chest containing your prize of 10,000 Gold Pieces. He then places a laurel wreath upon your head and proclaims you Champion of the Deathtrap Dungeon.
